about: Content fixes applied on top of the verified 3.29 research (guides-3.29.json stays the untouched record). tools/make_guides.py and tools/make_syndicate.py apply these in order before building; the format is documented in make_guides.py (apply_corrections). Map list checked 2026-11-04 against the 3.29.0 patch notes ('The following Maps have been removed from the Atlas: ...') and the PoE Wiki atlas_nodes table for the 3.29 series (Deepwater), which agree.

corrections.match: Use small, fast maps (Ashen Wood, Dunes, Strand).
corrections.value: Use small, fast maps (Dunes, Strand).
corrections.reason: Ashen Wood was removed from the Atlas in 3.29.0. Dunes and Strand are still on the 3.29 Atlas.

corrections.match: , and no Kirac mod helps.
corrections.value: . (Map Device crafts, Kirac's included, were removed in 3.28.)
corrections.reason: The line implied Kirac map mods still exist. 3.28.0 removed all Map Device crafting options.

corrections.match: Run T16 Carcass. Its narrow layout means fewer tendrils, so you hold more lanes.
corrections.value: 3.28 only: run T16 Carcass, whose narrow layout means fewer tendrils, so you hold more lanes. Carcass left the Atlas in 3.29; there, use Toxic Sewer, the best 3.29 Map Blight map in this guide.
corrections.reason: Carcass was removed from the Atlas in 3.29.0, so the first step of this 3.28 strategy can't be followed in 3.29. Toxic Sewer is on the 3.29 Atlas and is this guide's own top 3.29 Map Blight pick ('Map Blight on regular maps (3.29)').

corrections.match: Best map is Toxic Sewer, then Waste Pool.
corrections.value: Best map is Toxic Sewer. (Waste Pool, the old runner-up, has been off the Atlas since 3.28.)
corrections.reason: Waste Pool was removed from the Atlas in 3.28.0 and did not come back in 3.29.0 (not in the 3.29 add-back list, not on the 3.29 Atlas).

corrections.match: such as City Square, Mesa, Toxic Sewer, Ashen Wood and Canyon.
corrections.value: such as City Square, Mesa and Toxic Sewer.
corrections.reason: Ashen Wood and Canyon were removed from the Atlas in 3.29.0. City Square, Mesa and Toxic Sewer are on the 3.29 Atlas.

corrections.match: On T11+, also chisel to 20% quality and Vaal them.
corrections.value: On T11+, also Vaal them. (Cartographer's Chisels can no longer be obtained since 3.28, so the old chisel-to-20% step is gone.)
corrections.reason: 3.28.0: 'Cartographer's Chisels can no longer be obtained'. The guide's own Incursion changes already say chisel advice is out of date.

corrections.match: Caldera and Crimson Temple are alternatives.
corrections.value: Caldera is an alternative. (This 2024 guide also named Crimson Temple, which left the Atlas in 3.29.)
corrections.reason: Crimson Temple was removed from the Atlas in 3.29.0; Caldera is on the 3.29 Atlas.

value.title: Content Update 3.28.0 - Path of Exile: Mirage (patch notes)

corrections.reason: Source for the 3.28 Map Device craft removal (Kirac's Ultimatum mod).

corrections.match: Outdated guide: Maxroll's 2024 guide prices Kirac's Ultimatum mod at 5c.

value.text: Outdated guide: Maxroll's 2024 guide uses Kirac's Ultimatum map-device mod (5c). 3.26 cut it to 4c, and 3.28 removed all Map Device crafts, so it no longer exists.

corrections.reason: The line priced a mod that 3.28.0 removed, as if it still existed at 4c.

value.text: Map Device crafting was removed, so Kirac's Ultimatum map mod is gone.

corrections.reason: The Ultimatum changes stopped at the 3.26 price cut and never said the mod was removed.

corrections.match: You can roll Logbooks like maps, and split one into two with a Fenumal Plagued Arachnid at the Beastcrafting altar.
corrections.value: You can roll Logbooks like maps. They can no longer be split: 3.29 replaced the Beastcrafting split recipes with fracture crafts on Rare Talismans.
corrections.reason: 3.29.0: 'The Beastcrafting option to Split an item into two has been replaced with a new option that Fractures a Modifier on a Rare Talisman'. The Bestiary and Delve guides already say so.

corrections.match: After your last reroll, keep at least 2,000 Tribute. That is enough to defer the priciest rewards (about 20,000 at original cost).
corrections.value: After your last reroll, keep about 3,000 Tribute. Deferring costs 15% of the original price, so the priciest rewards (about 20,000) need about 3,000; 2,000 only covers items up to about 13,300.
corrections.reason: The guide's own deferral cost is 15% (10% plus a 5% fee); 15% of 20,000 is 3,000. The 2,000 figure dropped the fee.

corrections.match: Keep 2,000 Tribute after your last reroll so you can still defer.
corrections.value: Keep about 3,000 Tribute after your last reroll so you can still defer the priciest rewards (15% of about 20,000).
corrections.reason: Same 15% deferral arithmetic as the how-to line.

corrections.match: Reroll is 2,000. Keep 2,000 spare to defer.
corrections.value: Reroll is 2,000. Keep ~3,000 spare to defer.
corrections.reason: Same 15% deferral arithmetic as the how-to line.

corrections.match: The Timeless Splinter duplication gear mod was removed, along with white-socket and single-colour-socket enchants on rewards and Tailoring/Tempering Orbs.
corrections.value: The Timeless Splinter duplication gear mod was removed. White-socket and single-colour-socket enchantments no longer appear on Heist rewards or from Tailoring and Tempering Orbs; the orbs themselves remain.
corrections.reason: 3.29.0 only stops those enchantments from appearing on Heist rewards or from the orbs; the old wording read as if the orbs were removed, while the guide tells players to sell them.
